I want to tweak our Renovate config: Currently, Renovate opens at max 2 PRs per hour (and thus also at max 2 PRs *per run*), I think – with the consequence that only a subset of all pending updates are submitted within our `"after 8pm on sunday"`, `"before 8am on monday"` 12h-window. See our current [Dependency Dashboard](https://github.com/salim-b/home-assistant-apps-salim/issues/22) which lists 10 pending updates as "rate-limited" (4 updates got merged during the last 12h-window, the rest stayed pending).

I think we need to change Renovate's [`prHourlyLimit`](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#prhourlylimit) setting which defaults to `2` – we could simply disable that limit (`0`) unless there are compelling reasons not to.

Additionally, I think we should also increase [`prConcurrentLimit`](https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/#prconcurrentlimit) which defaults to `10` – I think 30 would be fine.

Please critically assess the situation and my proposal and then report back.

        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          repository: frenck/action-addon-linter
          ref: v2.21
          path: linter
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: 🐍 Install the linter requirements
        run: python3 -m pip install --no-cache-dir --prefer-binary -r linter/src/requirements.txt

      - name: 🚀 Run Home Assistant App Lint
        # lint.py reads its configuration from the GitHub action-input env convention (INPUT_*):
        # `path` is the app directory, `community` stays false (the action's default). The two
        # JSON schemas are loaded from absolute paths (the Docker image copied them to /) – provide them.
        env:
          # matrix values are plain strings (no JSON quoting) – safe to pass through env:.
          INPUT_PATH: ./${{ matrix.path }}
        run: |
          sudo cp linter/src/config.schema.json linter/src/build.schema.json /
          INPUT_COMMUNITY="false" \
            python3 linter/src/lint.py

  check:
    name: Mise check (lint + validate)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - name: ⤵️ Check out code from GitHub
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: ⚙️ Set up mise (installs pinned tools via mise.lock)
        uses: jdx/mise-action@d5574b52816a478f9d4e6529a3f6ff17a8a36785  # v5.2.8

      - name: ✅ Run mise tasks (lint + validate)
        # GITHUB_TOKEN enables zizmor's online-only audits (impostor-commit, known-vulnerable-actions,
        # ref-confusion, stale-action-refs); the default token's public-data reads suffice (rate
        # limit 1k req/hr per repo, a few dozen calls here). Tokenless runs fall back to offline.
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: mise run check

      - name: 🧭 Check apk pin drift
        # Alpine's binary indexes are world-state, not PR state: a repoint must not redden open
        # PRs (the bump automation resolves drift). Main pushes and the daily cron carry the
        # alarm; the PR gate's pin arbiter is the PR's own build (root KNOWLEDGE.md §"apk package version policy").
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: mise run validate:apk-pins

Title: Configuration Options - Mend Renovate CLI Docs
URL: https://docs.renovatebot.com/configuration-options/

**`prHourlyLimit`**
- Documented description: Rate limit PRs to maximum x created per hour. 0 means no limit.
- Default value: `2`
- Notes about "0 disables"/"0 means no limit": "0 means no limit."

**`prConcurrentLimit`**
- Documented description: Limit to a maximum of x concurrent branches/PRs. 0 means no limit.
- Default value: `10`
- Notes about "0 disables"/"0 means no limit": "0 means no limit."

**`branchConcurrentLimit`**
- Documented description: Limit to a maximum of x concurrent branches. 0 means no limit, `null` (default) inherits value from `prConcurrentLimit`.
- Default value: `null`
- Notes about "0 disables"/"0 means no limit": "0 means no limit"

**Relative Default Note:**
`null` (default) inherits value from `prConcurrentLimit`.

**Automerge PR Exemption Note:**
Renovate does not count or exempt PRs based on automerge in the descriptions of these specific limits; however, regarding concurrency limits and automerge/vulnerability alerts, the documentation notes: "By default, when Renovate creates a `vulnerabilityAlerts` PR, it ignores settings like `branchConcurrentLimit`, `commitHourlyLimit`, `prConcurrentLimit`, `prHourlyLimit`, or `schedule`."

## Verdict

Your proposal is sound – I'd make both changes. Facts gathered:

- Your `.github/renovate.json` sets no `prHourlyLimit`/`prConcurrentLimit` → defaults apply: **2/hour** and **10 concurrent**.
- Renovate runs via the **hosted Mend app** (the dashboard links to the Mend.io portal), on the free **Community Cloud** tier. - PR creation timestamps from the last window (Sun 22 Nov 20:00 → Mon 23 Nov 08:00 CET):

| Time (CET) | PRs created | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Sun 23:32 | #34 copilot, #35 ruff | one run, 2 PRs (hourly quota) |
| Mon 04:17 | – | #34/#35 automerged (GitHub native, checks green) |
| Mon 07:58 | #36 rumdl, #37 tombi | next productive run, 2 min before window close; still open |

So the mechanism is: `prHourlyLimit` is a rolling per-hour creation rate, not strictly per-run – but since the free tier only runs your repo every ~4 h, each run gets a fresh quota of 2. - **Org-wide job slot = 1**: other repos under `salim-b` running Renovate jobs serialize against yours, which is why runs that night were sparse and irregular.
- **Window-edge luck**: #36/#37 only exist because a run happened to land at 07:58, two minutes before close. A missed slot means updates wait a full week.

- Caveat from the docs (not relevant to you today): vulnerability-alert PRs ignore these limits entirely.

- No need to touch `branchConcurrentLimit`: it defaults to `null` and **inherits `prConcurrentLimit`** – it becomes 30 automatically.

  "platformAutomerge": true,
  "prHourlyLimit": 0,
  "prConcurrentLimit": 30,
  "rebaseWhen": "conflicted",
```

One nuance on timing: Renovate evaluates the schedule per update, and right now (Sunday 11:41) the window is *closed* – it reopens tonight at 20:00. Change and release discipline for this Home Assistant apps repository – branching, Conventional Commits, lint gates, the single-version-per-branch release rule with changelogs, CI-as-source-of-truth, device-access policy, and the version-sensitive-facts rule. Use before making any change, commit, or release in this repo.

## Content

# Change and release workflow

## Before starting

- Check the current branch first (`git status`): **Always work on a branch named `agent-<topic>`**, create one if needed
  (based off of `main`, i.e. `git switch -c agent-<topic> main`).
- If work belongs on a branch but a stray commit already landed on `main`: move it
  (`git switch -c agent-…; git branch -f main <upstream-tip>`) and disclose it to the user.
- Never stage unrelated WIP: check `git status` before staging and add files explicitly.

## Commits

- Conventional Commits (`build`, `chore:`, `ci`, `docs:`, `feat:`, `fix:`, `perf`, `refactor`, `revert`, `style`,
  `test`); scope app changes (`fix(nfs-server): …`); one commit per logical unit.
- Final trailer line: `Assisted-by: Goose:<model-slug>` – the model name without provider prefix, e.g.
  `Assisted-by: Goose:glm-5.3-flash`.
- The commit-msg hook enforces the format; escape hatch `HK=0 git commit`.

## Before finishing a change

Run `mise run check` – lint plus validate; it is the same gate CI runs. Lint-stack details and scoped checking: skill
`ha-app-tooling`. Task usage: `mise run check --help`.

## App releases

- A working branch starting from `main` bumps `version` in `config.yaml` to a **single** next version (major, minor or
  patch by semantic versioning): the branch ships one version, not one per commit, and continuously expands that
  version's `CHANGELOG.md` entry until it lands on `main`.
- Transitory extra versions within the branch are fine where testing demands one (AppArmor profile changes are only
  re-applied on app *update*, never on rebuild) – squash them back into the single version (config plus one merged
  changelog entry) before merging.
- CI enforces the rule: `.github/workflows/version-guard.yaml` fails when device-visible app files (`rootfs/`,
  `Dockerfile`, `config.yaml`, `apparmor.txt`, `translations/`) changed without a version bump – the Supervisor's update
  model makes a no-bump change a silent no-op that only repoints an already-published version tag. Exception: if the
  base version's GHCR tag was never published (its release's build/publish failed), the guard probes GHCR and passes –
  reusing the version then repoints nothing; unprovable fails closed. Changes to docs-only files (README, DOCS,
  CHANGELOG, KNOWLEDGE, TODO, `.agents/`), the per-app `.dockerignore` (it shapes the build context but never changes
  the image the device receives), and repo tooling do not require a version bump.

## CI/CD is the source of truth for what gets published

- Pushes to `main` build and publish images (`.github/workflows/builder.yaml`). If CI fails, fix the repo, not CI config
  – unless the CI config itself is wrong.
- Builder caveats: the init job needs `fetch-depth: 0` – the changed-files filter otherwise only sees the tip commit and
  silently skips multi-commit merges, so use regular merges instead of squash merges.
- The app `Dockerfile` must not pull from Docker Hub at build time (rule and rationale: skill `ha-app-scaffolding`).
- The lint workflow runs frenck's app linter natively (pinned source plus pypi requirements), not via its Docker action
  (whose Docker Hub image builds flaked with 504s and 429 runner-pool rate limits).
- In `.github/workflows/`, match GitHub users and bots by immutable user id, never by `login` (root `KNOWLEDGE.md`
  §"GitHub Actions: user identity matching").

## Device access

Testing against the real HA device over SSH only on explicit user request; otherwise hand the user exact commands to
run. On-device procedures: skill `ha-app-device-testing`.

## Version-sensitive facts

Supervisor schemas, s6-overlay layout, HAOS kernel configs and HA docs change frequently. Wherever such facts are
written down (`KNOWLEDGE.md`, comments, skills), cite the source (URL plus version/ref). Before relying on them for new
work, re-verify against the latest docs/source.

## Design change proposals

When a fix reveals a design issue, diagnose hands-on first (strace, packet captures, a reproduction lab), then explain
root cause, options and trade-offs to the user before rewriting.

## Text files

Every text file ends with a final newline (the lint gate enforces it).

- Conventional Commits (`build`, `chore:`, `ci`, `docs:`, `feat:`, `fix:`, `perf`, `refactor`, `revert`, `style`,
  `test`); scope app changes (`fix(nfs-server): …`); one commit per logical unit.
- Final trailer line: `Assisted-by: Goose:<model-slug>` – the model name without provider prefix, e.g.
  `Assisted-by: Goose:glm-5.3-flash`.
- The commit-msg hook enforces the format; escape hatch `HK=0 git commit`.

## Before finishing a change

Run `mise run check` – lint plus validate; it is the same gate CI runs. Lint-stack details and scoped checking: skill
`ha-app-tooling`. Task usage: `mise run check --help`.

## App releases

- A working branch starting from `main` bumps `version` in `config.yaml` to a **single** next version (major, minor or
  patch by semantic versioning): the branch ships one version, not one per commit, and continuously expands that
  version's `CHANGELOG.md` entry until it lands on `main`.
- Transitory extra versions within the branch are fine where testing demands one (AppArmor profile changes are only
  re-applied on app *update*, never on rebuild) – squash them back into the single version (config plus one merged
  changelog entry) before merging.
- CI enforces the rule: `.github/workflows/version-guard.yaml` fails when device-visible app files (`rootfs/`,
  `Dockerfile`, `config.yaml`, `apparmor.txt`, `translations/`) changed without a version bump – the Supervisor's update
  model makes a no-bump change a silent no-op that only repoints an already-published version tag. Exception: if the
  base version's GHCR tag was never published (its release's build/publish failed), the guard probes GHCR and passes –
  reusing the version then repoints nothing; unprovable fails closed. Changes to docs-only files (README, DOCS,
  CHANGELOG, KNOWLEDGE, TODO, `.agents/`), the per-app `.dockerignore` (it shapes the build context but never changes
  the image the device receives), and repo tooling do not require a version bump.

## CI/CD is the source of truth for what gets published

- Pushes to `main` build and publish images (`.github/workflows/builder.yaml`). If CI fails, fix the repo, not CI config
  – unless the CI config itself is wrong.
- Builder caveats: the init job needs `fetch-depth: 0` – the changed-files filter otherwise only sees the tip commit and
  silently skips multi-commit merges, so use regular merges instead of squash merges.
- The app `Dockerfile` must not pull from Docker Hub at build time (rule and rationale: skill `ha-app-scaffolding`).
- The lint workflow runs frenck's app linter natively (pinned source plus pypi requirements), not via its Docker action
  (whose Docker Hub image builds flaked with 504s and 429 runner-pool rate limits).
- In `.github/workflows/`, match GitHub users and bots by immutable user id, never by `login` (root `KNOWLEDGE.md`
  §"GitHub Actions: user identity matching").

## Device access

Testing against the real HA device over SSH only on explicit user request; otherwise hand the user exact commands to
run. On-device procedures: skill `ha-app-device-testing`.

## Version-sensitive facts

Supervisor schemas, s6-overlay layout, HAOS kernel configs and HA docs change frequently. Wherever such facts are
written down (`KNOWLEDGE.md`, comments, skills), cite the source (URL plus version/ref). Before relying on them for new
work, re-verify against the latest docs/source.

## Design change proposals

When a fix reveals a design issue, diagnose hands-on first (strace, packet captures, a reproduction lab), then explain
root cause, options and trade-offs to the user before rewriting.

## Text files

Every text file ends with a final newline (the lint gate enforces it).
